purpose: Hand-authored (Claude, not Gemini) multi-label requirements for the 'healthcare' domain, to teach the BERT classifier category semantics outside BFSI vocabulary. Every item is UNVERIFIED and needs a human label pass before it enters permanent training data.
instructions_for_reviewers: Confirm each 'categories' list against your project's 13-category definitions; add/remove labels.
Watch for over-labelling with 'Functional' -- keep it only where the system performs a concrete action.
'Regulatory' = a legal/standard mandate; 'Security' = protection mechanism. Don't conflate.
Single-label items are fine. Flip 'verified' to true only after a human check.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow a patient to book, reschedule, or cancel an appointment with a physician through a web or mobile interface.
The system shall verify a patient's insurance eligibility with the payer before confirming a scheduled procedure.
The system shall restrict access to a patient's medical record to clinicians involved in that patient's care.
The system shall obtain and record the patient's informed consent before any procedure and before sharing records with another provider.
The system shall keep an audit log of every access to a patient record, including the user, the time, and the records viewed.
The system shall encrypt all protected health information at rest and in transit in line with applicable health-data regulations.
The electronic health record system shall be available twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week, with unplanned downtime under fifteen minutes per month.
The system shall fail over to a standby site within ten minutes so that clinicians keep access to records during an outage.
The system shall retrieve and display a patient's complete medication history within three seconds of the record being opened.
The system shall alert the prescribing clinician when a new prescription conflicts with the patient's recorded allergies or current medications.
The system shall import laboratory test results from the laboratory information system and attach them to the correct patient record.
The system shall let a patient view their lab results, visit summaries, and prescriptions through a patient portal.
The system shall retain patient medical records for the minimum period required by law and prevent their deletion before that period expires.
The system shall allow a hospital administrator to configure appointment types, durations, and clinician availability without IT support.
The system shall generate the statutory disease-notification report and submit it to the public health authority within the mandated time.
The system shall support at least two thousand concurrent clinical users during peak outpatient hours without response times exceeding two seconds.
The system shall let a patient request a correction to their demographic or clinical information and route it to the records team for review.
The system shall de-identify patient data before releasing it to the analytics environment for research and reporting.
The system shall notify the on-call support team within five minutes if the interface engine stops processing inbound HL7 messages.
The system shall provide clinical staff a role-based dashboard summarising their patients' pending results, orders, and tasks.
The system shall recover clinical systems within a recovery time objective of one hour and a recovery point objective of five minutes after a declared disaster.
The system shall require multi-factor authentication for any access to the electronic health record from outside the hospital network.
The system shall bill the patient and the insurer for the correct co-payment and covered amount according to the plan's coverage rules.
The system shall keep an immutable record of every amendment to a clinical note, retaining the original text and the change history.
The system shall let authorised public health researchers query aggregate, non-identifiable statistics without access to individual records.
The system shall take backups of the clinical database every hour and verify the integrity of each backup.
The system shall present drug names, dosages, and instructions in language a patient can understand on the printed discharge summary.
The system shall reconcile admitted-patient counts between the registration and billing modules each night and report discrepancies.
The system shall allow emergency break-glass access to a record by a treating clinician, with mandatory reason capture and immediate notification to the privacy officer.
The system shall schedule downtime for upgrades only during a pre-announced low-activity window and provide clinical staff a documented downtime procedure.
